title: RpcContractSchema
description: Schema root, so one generated JSON Schema covers both directions of the wire.

deviceName.description: The creating physical device gets a new grant scoped to the new account.

SessionListRequest.description:
Sessions outlive their host's connection, so listing has to say which view is wanted.
The default is the console view: places you can actually send a command right now.

commandId.description: Idempotency key for a host command replayed from an offline outbox.

index.description:
Effective-queue position for the first added track. Absent appends. An insert keeps
the cursor on its occurrence, does not stop transport and is not reshuffled; the new
occurrences follow the preceding occurrence in original order.

sleepTimerId.description: Only stop if this timer is still armed. Local and backstop Stops share a receipt.

page.description: Resume only this source and result kind, with the same query. Absent fans out.

cursor.description: Opaque, expiring core-issued token. Return the whole page descriptor unchanged.

PluginValue.description:
JSON represented as a recursive, language-neutral sum type rather than `any`. This is
the input/output escape hatch for capability-specific operations while their envelopes
and failure behavior stay fully typed.

RpcStationSeed.description: What a station is started from. The kind must be one the source declared in `plugin.list`.

externalId.description: The source's reference for the seed, as it appeared in a search result.

StationSeedKind.description:
What a station can be started from.

A source declares the kinds it accepts so a client can offer "start a station here" only
where it works. `Album` is in the vocabulary because the library is album-centric, and no
shipped plugin accepts it yet: declaring support is exactly how that stays visible instead
of being discovered through a failed call.

cursor.description: The cursor from the previous batch. Absent asks for the first batch.

RpcSystemStatus.description:
Service health and capability summary.

`pluginCount` and `capabilities` are part of status because the core is required to run
with zero plugins installed. A client discovers what is actually possible here rather
than assuming a provider exists.

capabilities.description:
Capability classes currently served by at least one live plugin, for example
`source` or `output`. Empty is a valid, working state.

RpcFailure.description:
Uniform failure envelope.

`retryable` exists so an offline client can decide whether to keep a queued write or
surface it as a permanent error, without parsing `code` strings.

bearerToken.description: Returned exactly once. Clients persist this in their local ProseQL worker store.

isDefault.description:
True for the account created automatically on first boot. Exactly one account
carries this flag.

bearerToken.description: Returned once; only its hash is stored.

stationSeedKinds.description:
Seed kinds this source accepts for `source.station.create`. Empty for a plugin that is
not a source, and for a source whose stations cannot be derived from a seed.

queueOrder.description:
Occurrence ordinals in effective queue order. Ascending order restores the original
queue, even when the same track occurs more than once. Absent implies 0..queue.len.

oneOf.description:
Delivered to the host. The resulting state arrives as a realtime event, not here:
only the host can say what actually happened to its audio.

The host is not connected. The command is refused rather than queued, because a
command applied minutes later is not what the person pressing the button meant.

The host is connected but is not draining commands. Refused so a wedged renderer
cannot turn a console into an unbounded write amplifier.

The command reports what the host's audio actually did. Only the host may say that
about itself, so it cannot be issued from a console.

The source host is not connected, so it cannot be told to stop. Its audio may still
be playing, and moving the queue anyway is how two rooms end up playing at once.

The target already holds a queue. Refused rather than silently overwriting music
somebody is listening to.
Output sessions require speaker effects and are not moved by device handoff.

RpcSourceSearchResult.description:
Every kind a discovery search can return. A source that cannot answer one kind
contributes the kinds it can and appears in no failure, because an unimplemented
operation is a capability boundary rather than a provider fault.

pages.description: One next page per source and kind that supplied a continuation.

externalId.description:
The source's own reference for this recording. It addresses `source.station.create`
with a `track` seed, so a client can start a station from a song it just found.
Without it a client can list and play stations but can never begin one.

albumExternalId.description:
The source's reference for the album this recording belongs to, when it has one.
It addresses `source.album.get`, so a client can open the album behind a song.

RpcStationListResult.description: Stations gathered from every live source, with per-source failures beside them.

RpcStation.description:
A radio object owned by a source.

One shape covers a Pandora station token and a YouTube Music watch queue, which is the
point: a client renders a station without knowing which provider produced it. Provider
concepts that do not fit, such as Pandora's QuickMix flag, are deliberately absent until
the model grows to hold them.

externalId.description:
The source's own reference. Opaque to the core and to clients; only the owning plugin
interprets it.

SourceStationCreateOutcome.description:
`unsupportedSeed` is a capability boundary, not a fault. A source that cannot build a
station from this kind of seed said so in `plugin.list`, and answering with a failure
would put an error beside an honest refusal.

cursor.description: Opaque, expiring core-issued cursor for the next batch of this station.

RpcProtocolFailureOutcome.description:
A request that cannot enter operation dispatch. This is separate from an operation's
`unavailable` outcome: no operation exists yet to own the failure.

RealtimeHello.description:
The first message on every socket.

Browsers cannot set an `Authorization` header when opening a WebSocket, and a query
string would copy the bearer token into proxy and server logs. An explicit hello frame
keeps the token in the message body, where the RPC transport already keeps it.

resumeToken.description: Opaque cursor from a previous `welcome` or `event`. Absent on a first connection.

RpcRealtimeTopic.description:
Realtime fan-out topics.

A subscription is always scoped to the authenticated account, so a topic name can never
widen visibility beyond it. Each topic maps to the same scope its RPC read operations
require, so a token cannot watch what it may not read.

oneOf.description:
Acknowledges a subscribe or unsubscribe and carries the resulting topic set. A
client can wait for this before assuming a subscription change has taken effect.
A console asked this device to change one of its sessions.
Terminal. The socket closes immediately after this frame.

resumeToken.description: Opaque cursor to send on the next reconnect. Clients must not parse it.

resumed.description: True when a resume token was accepted and missed events were replayed below.

missedEventsDropped.description:
True when the requested resume point had already been evicted. The client must
refetch state through RPC instead of trusting the replay to be complete.

RpcRealtimeState.description:
Published state. Every variant carries the whole record rather than a delta, so a
client that misses an event and refetches converges on the same value.

RpcSessionDirective.description:
A command routed to the device that hosts a session.

The core never applies a console command itself. The host owns transport truth, so it
applies the command and reports the result through `session.command.run`, which is what
fans the new state back out.

expectedRevision.description: Seek is fenced to the session revision observed when it was routed.

issuedBy.description: The device or token that asked. Present so a host can show who is driving it.

directiveId.description:
Unique per directive. A host that reconnects mid-delivery can discard a repeat
rather than adding the same tracks to its queue twice.

config.description:
Decrypted per-account config. It exists only in this request and plugin memory;
plaintext is never stored in ProseQL or logged by core.

configSchema.description: JSON Schema for per-account plugin configuration and credentials.

source.description:
Declared source abilities. Absent for a plugin that contributes no `source` capability,
and absent for an older source plugin that predates the declaration.

SourceFeatures.description:
Source abilities that an operation name alone cannot express.

A plugin that implements `station.create` still cannot say which seeds it accepts.
Probing every kind against every source on every render is the cost this removes, and
`plugin.list` is the one place a third-party client has to look.

stationSeedKinds.description:
Seed kinds `station.create` accepts. Empty is honest for a provider whose stations are
all account-owned and cannot be derived from something you point at.
